author: BeauHD
description: Google is shutting down its 15-year-old Nest app on January 25, 2027, requiring users to switch to Google Home to remotely control their smart home devices and receive notifications. "Then, on August 2, the company will retire Google Assistant on smart speakers and displays, with Gemini replacing the older tech for voice controls," reports Engadget. From the report: If you've yet to migrate your Nest devices to the Google Home app, the company says your existing settings and schedules will transfer over automatically. The only thing you need to manually move over are any custom clips you might have saved over the years. You can do this by visiting the Nest website before January 25 and clicking the "Download all" button. Google says it will automatically migrate Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions to its newer Google Home Premium package. "You will receive an email closer to the date of transfer detailing your subscription information," the company adds. "The Nest app launched over 15
title: Google Is Finally Retiring the Nest App Early Next Year

author: BeauHD
description:
President Trump has ordered the military to halt plans to detonate nearly five tons of unstable lead azide explosives at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa. "Trump claimed that the fate of the unstable, highly explosive material is now in the hands of a federal court and Rob Sand, Iowa's governor-elect, who won't be sworn into office until January," reports Ars Technica. From the report: The Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The explosion will launch a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could reach up to 100 miles away from the Iowa facility, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP).
 
Iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand. The environmental groups, led by Earthjustice, claimed in an emergency court filing that the Army had not fully considered safer options for disposing of the lead azide before
title: Trump Halts Army's Plans to Detonate Bomb-Making Chemicals In Iowa

author: BeauHD
description: Anthropic has unveiled Claude Ship, a new feature in Claude Code that allows AI agents to review pull requests, fix bugs, resolve merge conflicts and approve code changes according to policies established by development teams. 9to5Mac reports: Claude Ship is comprised of three agents: Code Review, PR Steward, and Claude Approvals. "Together, they take a pull request through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don't have to manage each step manually," Anthropic says. "Developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests with the new /ship command in Claude Code," Anthropic says.
title: Anthropic Launches Claude Ship to Review, Fix, and Approve Code

author: BeauHD
description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang received a standing ovation from employees upon returning to the company's headquarters Monday, less than two weeks after resigning amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy. "Thank you all for the second chances. I'm gonna be a better CEO the second time around," Huang told staff. His reinstatement followed intervention by President Trump and Vice President JD Vance, with Nvidia's board saying it received assurances from senior U.S. officials that Huang's return posed no national security risk.
title: Jensen Huang Says He'll Be a 'Better CEO' As Staff Applauds His Return

author: BeauHD
description:
CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire network security provider Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal. "The deal marks CrowdStrike's biggest acquisition to date and is among the largest in the sector as businesses consolidate and ramp up defenses to fend off AI-powered attacks," reports CNBC. The acquisition is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028. From the report: "With Zscaler, we're building cybersecurity's operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely," CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said in a statement. "We see a path to become the largest AI safety and security company the world has ever seen."
 
CrowdStrike has been a major beneficiary of skyrocketing demand for AI security, with shares soaring about 80% this year as of Monday's open. Zscaler shares are up about 5% year to date after Monday's surge. Their combined market value exceeded $265 billion as of Friday's close, behind marke
title: CrowdStrike to Buy Zscaler In $44 Billion Deal

author: BeauHD
description: President Trump reportedly directed a behind-the-scenes effort to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO, enlisting Vice President JD Vance to secure assurances from federal officials that Huang was not facing criminal charges or considered a national security risk. According to The New York Times, the intervention came despite intelligence concerns surrounding Huang's alleged relationship with a suspected Chinese spy linked to an investigation into illegal Nvidia chip shipments to China. From the report: [...] Only a tiny handful of officials at the highest level of the government were aware of these conversations. On Sunday night, Nvidia's board told the administration that it would be announcing Mr. Huang's reinstatement on Monday morning before the markets opened. The announcement included a note about a new compliance committee, intended to offer public assurance that the company was taking seriously the investigation into the possible smuggling of advanced chips. Mr. Trump was s
title: Trump Is Said to Have Directed Effort to Reinstate Nvidia Chief

author: BeauHD
description:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from Wired: At 16 years old, Henrijs Dandzbergs is too young to vote. Or drink. Or smoke. Or drive unsupervised. But he's not too young to win half a million dollars for his AI-guided-missile startup. In September, Dandzbergs, who was born in Latvia, was admitted to Y Combinator's fall 2026 cohort. The startup accelerator counts companies like Airbnb, Stripe, DoorDash, and Reddit among its alumni; Dandzbergs is likely the youngest solo founder in its vaunted history. His startup, Polemos Industries, is attempting to develop a new class of precision-guided missile that can be easily and cheaply manufactured, can be fired from portable launchers, and can resist jamming attempts. "I think missiles are the coolest thing," Dandzbergs tells WIRED. "A lot of people that have found success in engineering early on have had a passion for blowing stuff up."
 
In conversation, Dandzbergs is poised and articulate. He talks about "attacking hard problems," breaki
title: YC Startup Working On 'Cost Per Kill' For Missiles

author: BeauHD
description:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Sunday that Americans should expect more technology outages as companies and government agencies modernize aging infrastructure. Speaking on CNN, Clayton said the upgrades are necessary to improve performance and cybersecurity but will inevitably cause "glitches, gaps, [and] interruptions in service." Reuters reports: A string of technology failures this month disrupted critical U.S. systems, including a nationwide halt to air travel, a Microsoft outage that hit email services, a technical glitch that affected several major banks, and a temporary disruption to the National Security Agency's network.
 
Speaking on the ABC program "This Week," Clayton reiterated his previous statements that those outages were not the result of coordinated or state-sponsored actions, attributing them to technical upgrades. Clayton declined to discuss specifics of separate reports of cyberattacks on the FBI and Department of Agriculture, saying he expec
title: US Intelligence Chief Predicts More Tech Outages As Systems Undergo Upgrades

author: BeauHD
description: Zak3056 shares a report from CNBC: Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked tech and artificial intelligence industries. The board of directors said it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him. The board added that it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" that it is confident that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk."
title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang As CEO

author: EditorDavid
description:
The Washington Post looks at Anthropic's "unique" corporate culture, where CEO Dario Amodei "leads his workforce through essays, long memos posted in Slack and twice-monthly all-hands talks jokingly known as 'Dario Vision Quests'... 

"The CEO's output has established a constellation of beliefs treated as obvious, urgent and righteous inside the company: AI that supersedes humans is inevitable, the United States must limit China's AI development, and Claude might be conscious."

Inside this tight-knit culture, Anthropic staffers, who call themselves Ants, get to feel that they are working on the world's most urgent problems, with the smartest people, in a shared mission to safeguard humanity, according to interviews with more than a dozen people familiar with the company's ethos, including several current and former employees. At its core is a belief that Anthropic — and Amodei — know what's best for the world... "A pervasive thing at Anthropic is: We're going to put on ou
title: Anthropic's Safety-Conscious Corporate Culture Still Envisions Superintelligent AI

author: EditorDavid
description:
Reuters reports:


Alice Huang, the Chinese woman at the heart of Nvidia's recent scandal, kept in contact with an official from China's top spy agency for more than a year during her affair with former CEO Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday. Alice Huang was in touch with an officer from China's Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the report said, citing people with knowledge of intelligence reports that describe the encounters... 

The scandal has also prompted a deeper look at Washington's approach to export controls on China, with lawmakers from both parties questioning whether the Trump administration has been too lax on enforcement and regulation of the prized semiconductors.
 
Reuters points out that several U.S. officials "have cast doubt on initial suggestions that Alice Huang was a spy..." 

"A spokesperson for Jensen Huang declined to comment. Spokespeople for Nvidia and the Chinese embassy in Washington did not im
title: Alice Huang In Touch With Chinese Spy Agency During Affair With Nvidia CEO, NYT Says

author: EditorDavid
description:
Last year Slashed reported that the privacy- and security-focused Android fork GrapheneOS was "partnering with a major Android OEM to bring its hardened, de-Googled OS to Snapdragon-powered flagship phones." 
 And early this November Motorola announced their upcoming high end Signature 27 phone would include official support for GrapheneOS as an OS option, the first Motorola device supporting GrapheneOS. 

But the nonprofit GrapheneOS project has a new problem, reports the blog It's FOSS :


GrapheneOS has accused Google of leaning on phone makers to keep away from the project. The claim came in a thread on X [Thursday], where the project says makers were questioned about working with it, then threatened over their Google app licensing.... The project says Google is working against GrapheneOS itself and expects it to go further. title: GrapheneOS Accuses Google of Kneecapping Its Android Partners Using Pixel Exclusives

author: EditorDavid
description:
"A number of ports across the U.S. are reporting an onslaught of cyberattacks," reports The Hill, "amid a growing number of AI-enabled attacks targeting notable infrastructure."


The Port of Corpus Christi, Texas, which functions as the U.S.'s largest passage of oil exports, said it was targeted with "hundreds if not thousands" of attacks per day, according to reporting from the Financial Times. The port's chief executive, Kent Britton, told the outlet that attacks surged from "known bad actor" countries and organizations that are searching for high-profile targets. ["Experts link countries like Iran, North Korea and China to hacking operations targeting shipping infrastructure," the Financial Times reports.] The attacks against Corpus Christi's port went after its computer systems by attempting to find weaknesses. Attackers also sent phishing messages, posing as senior executives, to trick staff into allowing them access, per the Financial Times... 

"They're poking at our systems a
title: America's Shipping Ports Now Face Thousands of Cyberattacks Each Day
